newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Emmanuelli says little scope on budget.
newsitem.headline: France's Emmanuelli says little scope on budget.

text.p: French National Assembly finance committee head Henri Emmanuelli said on Tuesday the government had little room for manoeuvre on the budget due to insufficient revenue and urged the adoption of carefully targeted stimulative measures.

"I don't have all the facts on the budget situation but it doesn't seem very good. I think revenue is falling short ... because of insufficient economic activity and growth," he told France Inter radio.

He urged the government to avoid broad-brush measures. "On value-added tax, rather than a generalised cut (in the basic rate) to five percent from 5.5, which wouldn't have much economic, political or social impact, I think it would be better to target ... sectors (such as) housing to give a little push to growth," he said.

During the recent election campaign which brought the Socialists to power, the party talked of cutting the basic rate of VAT which is levied on such goods as bread and milk to five percent from 5.5 percent.
Economists have calculated such a move would cost five billion francs ($850 million) in lost tax revenue.
The standard rate of VAT was raised by two percentage points by the previous conservative government to 20.6 percent.
